summary.text: Caesar's heir whom Ovid sets as the greater guardian of the conquered earth while the deified dictator watches from the sky — the Roman frame that closes the Metamorphoses.

story.text: The poem ends not on the deified dictator but on his heir: Augustus greater than his father, guarding the conquered earth while Caesar watches from the sky.

Ovid's Metamorphoses — begun with Chaos and gods — closes with the Roman frame that makes change the law of empire as well as of myth. Pythagoras' lesson that nothing dies prepares the reader for a metamorphosis that needs no heifer-form or spider-thread — only comet-fire and imperial succession.
